draft.title: What size backpack you need for a weekend
draft.metaDescription: Which pack capacity suits a two- or three-night trip, and when to size up.
draft.intro: For two or three nights, 38 litres is the size to buy, and the Weekender 38 is built for exactly that trip. A 22-litre daypack will not hold a sleeping bag; a 65-litre pack will hold everything you own and tempt you to bring it.

sections.heading: Why 38 and not 30 or 50
sections.body: The Weekender 38 carries 38 litres at 1.1 kg and takes a hip belt and a rain cover. That combination is what makes a weekend load sit on your hips instead of your shoulders. The Daypack 22 has neither, which is the real limit rather than its 22 litres.

sections.heading: When to size up
sections.body: Carrying a tent, or walking somewhere cold enough to need a four-season bag, pushes you past 38 litres. The Expedition 65 is 1.9 kg in cordura with pole loops — heavier and more pack than a weekend needs, and the right answer the moment the trip stops being a weekend.

sections.heading: What the litre number does not tell you
sections.body: Two 38-litre packs can carry differently depending on where the weight sits. A hip belt moves load off the shoulders; without one, capacity stops being useful well before the pack is full.
